mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations rise sharply as measured by CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers within 2 months after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or unemployment falls sharply within the forecast horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the decline in INDPRO reverses within the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below its 12-month average within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) after two consecutive quarters of decline signals renewed consumer confidence and spending, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 posts two consecutive quarterly increases after two quarters of decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered recoveries, or the GDP rebound is not sustained beyond the forecast horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., more people in the labor force but unemployment rising) signals labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate cost discipline, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month AND UNRATE increases month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or labor market conditions tighten within the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the decline in housing starts reverses within the forecast horizon.
